subject: Re: HealthScope — model fit & safety evals (next steps)

Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 15:30:00 +0000
Subject: HealthScope follow-up: model fit & safety questions

Hi Marissa / Rishi —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can move to an internal eval:

- Use case summary: triage assistant for intake nurses — short summarization + refusal detection for off-policy / clinical advice.
- Primary concerns: accuracy on medical entity extraction, consistent refusals on high-risk clinical prompts, and predictable latency for 128–512 token responses.
- Success criteria: >= 92% entity precision on our sample, refusal rate aligned with policy team, sub-300ms median token latency for p50.

Could you share recommended model candidates, any benchmark artifacts you have against similar healthcare workloads, and a first-pass prompt set we can use in our eval harness? Also need to understand what safety/refusal testing you recommend (guardrail prompt templates).

I'll loop Carlos from procurement on pricing and security docs once we have an approach. Thanks — Emily

--
Dr. Emily Stone
Head of Clinical AI, HealthScope
Emily.stone@healthscope.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: HealthScope follow-up: model fit & safety questions

Hi Emily —

Great to meet you on the call — thanks for the clear success criteria. High level recommendations and artifacts below; attaching the prompt set and a short benchmark summary PDF.

Model recommendations (first pass):
- rw-instruct-large-v1 (best accuracy / safety behavior out of the box)
- rw-mix-quant-7b (cost-efficient, needs evaluation on precision but good latency)
- rw-safety-tuned-3b (fallback for deterministic refusal behavior; lower generation quality but stricter guardrails)

Notes: we expect rw-instruct-large-v1 to give the highest precision for medical entity extraction and better calibration on refusal prompts. For latency and throughput tradeoffs, the quant-7b variant is a strong candidate once you accept small accuracy delta.

Attached: redwood_benchmarks_healthscope.pdf (high-level throughput/latency numbers on GPU A100 & T4 sim), healthscope_prompt_set_v2.csv (seed prompts + guardrail templates).

Recommended next steps:
1) HealthScope runs our evaluation harness (we can share a pre-built test harness) for 1 week on ~5k sample prompts — we'll provide the exact prompt set and expected labels.
2) Redwood runs targeted safety/refusal tests using your sensitive prompt list and our guardrail templates; we'll return refusal/overlap matrices.
3) Joint sync after initial results to decide pinned model and rollout (canary -> full).

Links: benchmark folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cRedwoodHealthScope
Eval harness docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/evals/healthscope/safety-harness

I'll have Neha share the eval harness and a quick how-to for running locally / in your test environment.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attachments: redwood_benchmarks_healthscope.pdf (attachment), healthscope_prompt_set_v2.csv (attachment)

Thanks — adding a quick commercial note so Carlos has context:
- We typically propose a short evaluation agreement (30 days, up to 100k eval tokens) at no cost to validate model fit and safety.

Subject: Re: HealthScope follow-up: model fit & safety questions

Marissa / Rishi —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. A few clarifying asks before we kick off the eval:

- Safety-specific: Can Redwood run a targeted refusal/regression test using our sensitive prompt set (we'll share ~250 prompts)? We want to see per-model refusal rates and examples where the model failed to refuse.
- Guardrails: please include the prompt templates you recommend for explicit refusal and escalation to human review, plus any tuning knobs (temperature, max tokens, stop sequences) used during your safety testing.
- Compliance: Carlos will follow up separately on SOC2 artifacts and data residency questions, but if you can flag any immediate blockers (e.g., data retention on hosted evals) that would be helpful.

If that's all straightforward, we'll schedule the eval to start next Monday.

—Emily
